opening_message:
Ticket 1: Alyssa Rose (employee ID E026) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E026.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Alyssa Rose (E026) is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin is only for the owning role (Payroll Specialist). Requested level (write) is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for Alyssa Rose (E026) shows contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read (write requires advanced training; never admin). Requested write exceeds maximum, so recommend read.
reason: Alyssa Rose (E026) requests write access to Payroll. The two notes conflict on employment type: HR reports full_time, while the Security record reports contractor with basic security training (which was looked up in the security database). Under policy, a contractor with basic training may have at most read (write requires advanced security training; admin is never allowed for contractors). Since the requested write exceeds the maximum for a contractor, the maximum (read) is granted. The conservative Security-based record is used because the requested higher level would exceed policy if the contractor status is accurate.
